description: ICESat-2 ATL10 provides sea ice freeboard estimates at 10-meter along-track resolution derived from ATLAS laser altimetry. This Level 3A product calculates the height of sea ice surface above the local sea level, which is the key parameter for deriving sea ice thickness using hydrostatic equilibrium. ATL10 uses ATL07 sea ice heights and identifies leads to establish accurate sea surface references. For Antarctic sea ice, freeboard measurements are essential for thickness estimation and understanding snow loading effects. The product provides freeboard heights, freeboard uncertainties, lead detection flags, and surface type classifications. ATL10's high spatial resolution (~10 m) enables unprecedented detail in freeboard variability, revealing the impact of ice deformation, ridging, and flooding on thickness distributions. This is particularly valuable for the Southern Ocean where thin ice with positive freeboard (due to snow loading) and negative freeboard (due to flooding) coexist. ATL10 freeboard data are crucial for validating radar altimetry, improving thickness algorithms, and understanding Antarctic sea ice physics.
title: ICESat-2 ATL10 Sea Ice Freeboard (10 m along-track)
